WEBSEARCH VERIFICATION (trino.io/docs/current/functions/string.html + trino.io/docs/current/connector/iceberg.html, 2026-06-06):
  - `translate(source, from, to) -> varchar` — CONFIRMED: 'Replaces characters found in the from string with corresponding characters in the to string.' EXACT 1:1 of Oracle TRANSLATE.
  - `reverse(string) -> varchar` — CONFIRMED: 'Returns the input with characters in reverse order.'
  - `position(substring IN string) -> bigint` — CONFIRMED: 'Returns the starting position of the first instance of a substring. Positions start at 1; returns 0 if not found.'
  - `strpos(string, substring) -> bigint` — CONFIRMED same return semantics as position.
  - `levenshtein_distance(string1, string2) -> bigint` — CONFIRMED: 'Computes the minimum number of single-character edits needed to transform one string into another.'
  - `concat_ws(separator, string1, ..., stringN) -> varchar` — **CONFIRMED PRESENT IN TRINO 467** per docs and WebSearch corroboration across Trino 350-481 versions. 'Joins multiple strings using a separator, skipping any null values in the arguments.' The earlier r27 bans (lines 1212/1229/1360) claiming concat_ws is Postgres/Spark-only were FACTUALLY WRONG and have been reconciled.
